messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: git local files disappearing?
parts:
Hi all,

Sorry for an off-topic question, but I don't have a clue what's wrong
with my git setup and it's proving quite counter-productive. For two
days now I boot up the computer and find that the local directory
where I'd commited changes and pushed to github has vanished from my
computer (Mac OSX leopard). I definitely didn't rm the content myself,
and in fact, ggplot2_0.9.0.tar.gz still exists there after I built it
yesterday. "Only" the source code and the (hidden) .git directory have
disappeared, they're not even in the Trash.

Is this normal? Has anyone encountered this issue?

Thanks,

baptiste

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: git local files disappearing?
parts:
This sounds very strange - I've never heard of something like this happening with git. There are a few possibilities I can think of:
- Your filesystem is damaged
- A scheduled job is deleting the files (check the modification time of the directory to see when the deletion happens)
- A file sync program (like Dropbox) is getting confused and removing the files
- If you're browsing to the files from Finder, the files may have some attribute set that makes them hidden (but I think they should still be visible from the command line)

-Winston
